newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Traders cheer low Philippines' 20-yr bond coupon.
newsitem.headline: Traders cheer low Philippines' 20-yr bond coupon.

text.p: The investment community was pleased with the Philippines' first 20-year Treasury bond on Tuesday even though the yield was well below expectations, bank treasurers said.
The coupon of 14.375 percent, compares to predictions of between 14.5 to 16.0 percent.
"I don't think it's too low," Patrick Dewilde, vice president and head of financial markets of Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd, told reporters.
Dewilde said he had met several foreign investors who were interested in buying the 20-year fixed-rate bonds, the longest maturing government securities in the region.
"Clearly, there's a lot of investors standing behind the bidding banks," Dewilde said.
Total bids amounted to 12.87 billion pesos, but the auction committee awarded only 2.0 billion pesos worth of bonds.
Accepted bids ranged from 13.50 percent to 14.450 percent. However, all the bidders will get a uniform coupon of 14.375 percent based on the bidding rules.
"We have a very successful offering," Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said after emerging from the auction room.
He attributed the relativley low yield to the confidence of the investing public that the stable low interest rate regime would be sustained over the long term.
Philippine treasurer Caridad Valdehuesa said the new issue would further deepen the domestic capital market.
The auction committee was expecting bids to range from 15.0 to 16.0 percent, de Ocampo said.

"It's a demonstration of confidence that the people have in the Philippines. And I think it is a very well deserved confidence," Mark Boyne, vice president of Treasury and Capital Market of Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd, told Reuters.
The coupon rate was slightly higher than the prevailing 10-year fixed-rate Treasury bond rate which is trading at 13.5 percent in the secondary market.
Cesar Santos, president of the Money Market Association of the Philippines, said the coupon has kept the long yield curve relatively flat which is similar with its southeast Asian neighbours.
"This is an improvement for us. For a time, we were the only country which has a steep yield curve," Santos said.
Dewilde said the secondary market for the new issue would also be active, given the oversubscription of more than 10 billion pesos.

However, Vicente Panlilio, executive vice president and treasurer of Far East Bank and Trust Co, said the bank would probably keep the issue for themselves considering that the maiden issues have always yielded the best rate.
"We will keep it for ourselves, if we win," he said.
Traders also dismissed fears that the appetite would be easily satiated after a couple of auctions. The 20-year bonds would be offered every six months.
Boyne cited the case of the ten-year bond which was launched late last year which has been receiving a lot of interests in the secondary market.
Traders have been asking for higher offer size in the coming auctions.
